incident-bot: [PAGER] P1: policy-engine runtime panic — smart-routing fallbacks thrashing (auto-page sent) :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4107. Auto-escalation to #incidents and paging oncall.

maria (oncall): acknowledging — looking now. any quick impact summary?

liz (eng-runtime): seeing repeated policy eval panics from policy-service v2.3.1 -> stack traces show nil deref in rule compile path. This causes router to mark node as unhealthy and trigger region fallback loops between us-west-2 <-> eu-west-1 for some customers.

kevin (eng-sre): confirmed — load spikes and increased 502/503 from router for ~2 mins, then retries route to fallback region, which trips capacity checks and causes more retries. Looks like request_id sampling shows ~8% of traffic hitting fallback loop at peak.

maria (oncall): customer impact? any high-visibility tenants?

emily (support): ACME-Analytics reported timeouts and partial responses for embeddings batch jobs. Their logs show repeated discover_and_route errors and tokenization timeouts.

jay (product): noticed increased error rates on hosted API for embedding endpoints from Europe. Possibly correlated. Cross-checking now with observability.

liz (eng-runtime): pasted a representative stack (sanitized):
```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 72 [running]:
github.com/redwood/policyengine/eval.(*Compiler).compileRule(0xc0001f4000, 0xc000a3f200, 0x2a)
\t/go/src/policyengine/eval/compiler.go:214 +0x35d
github.com/redwood/policyengine/eval.(*Compiler).Compile(0xc0001f4000, 0xc000b7d000, 0x1, 0x1)
\t/go/src/policyengine/eval/compiler.go:112 +0x1b2
...
```

liz (eng-runtime): root cause appears to be an unguarded reference in the policy expression compiler when a rule contains an unexpected `nil` constant in an array literal. The policy YAML had a dynamic expression generated by the UI that produced `rules: - allowed_regions: [null]`. The compiler didn't validate and panicked.

maria (oncall): is there a quick mitigation we can do at router level to stop the fallback thrash?

liz (eng-runtime): yes — options: 1) temporarily pin affected customers to model-variant `v1-safe` via routing override API; 2) disable smart-routing for the entire region; 3) disable policy engine for routing (fall back to static routing table). Recommend 1 + 2 short-term.

kevin (eng-sre): I'll apply a routing override for ACME-Analytics and a small cohort to break the loop. Running command now.

kevin (eng-sre): ran:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/routing/overrides" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" -d '{"customer_id":"acme-analytics","override_variant":"v1-safe","expires_in":900}'
```

kevin (eng-sre): override ack'd by controlplane, responses for ACME now stable in metrics. Latency falling back to baseline.

maria (oncall): great. can we also disable smart-routing in eu-west-1 until we patch?

liz (eng-runtime): I'll flip the smart-routing toggle for eu-west-1 now (2 min downtime expected for the routing daemon to refresh).

liz (eng-runtime): toggled: `smart_routing.enabled = false` for eu-west-1 via infra console. Watch metrics.

kevin (eng-sre): seeing fallback loop stop — retries drop to 0. Error rate decreasing.

maria (oncall): creating a short-lived incident status update for customers: "The team is mitigating a policy engine runtime error affecting routing in EU/US regions; targeted mitigations applied; service is recovering." I'll send it in 10.

jay (product): good. we should notify some enterprise customers on guardrails we've applied (overrides) and that we will roll a policy patch.

liz (eng-runtime): root cause policy snippet (redacted):
```yaml
rules:
  - name: region_allowlist
    allowed_regions: [ null ]  # generated by malformed UI flow when country selector was cleared
    expr: "in(region, allowed_regions)"
```

liz (eng-runtime): compiler didn't validate `allowed_regions` length or element types before building AST; fix in patch: add validation and defensive nil checks.

maria (oncall): assign owners + timeline?

liz (eng-runtime): I'll cut a hotfix branch, running tests locally now. If green, will promote to canary in 15m and full rollout in 45m.

kevin (eng-sre): I'll keep overrides in place and hold smart-routing disabled until patch fully rolled.

emily (support): ACME support ticket updated with mitigation notes and ETA for fix. They asked for a brief RCA after.

maria (oncall): paging note: if latency >500ms or error rate >2% in the next 30m, escalate to P1-war room.

liz (eng-runtime): tests passed locally. pushing hotfix: `policy-compiler: add nil guards + validation`

liz (eng-runtime): promoting canary to 10% in us-west-2 first.

kevin (eng-sre): canary looks healthy 5m in — no panics, routing stable for the canary cohort.

liz (eng-runtime): starting full rollout.

kevin (eng-sre): full rollout complete. no regressions seen in the last 10m.

maria (oncall): smart-routing re-enabled for eu-west-1.

maria (oncall): monitoring for 30m, then we'll update status to "resolved" with follow-up RCA. Great work.

jay (product): follow-ups: add UI validation to prevent empty/nulls in allowed_regions, audit existing policies for `null` entries, add a regression test to the policy-eval harness.

liz (eng-runtime): filed PR: https://git.internal/redwood/policyengine/pulls/512 (hotfix + tests).

maria (oncall): noting timeline for incident postmortem:
- 2101012345: pager triggered; policy-engine panic observed
- 2101012352: overrides applied for affected customers
- 2101012360: smart-routing disabled in eu-west-1
- 2101012390: hotfix canary promoted
- 2101012442: full rollout complete; smart-routing re-enabled
- 2101012460: service stabilized; monitoring window started

maria (oncall): assigning postmortem to liz (eng-runtime) and kevin (eng-sre). Emily will draft customer-facing RCA.

emily (support): will coordinate ACME follow-up and send template RCA.

maria (oncall): closing pager channel once monitoring window passes. Thanks all :heart: 

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-4107 status -> mitigated (customer impact limited; hotfix deployed).
